title.raw: 卷1 序紀 Volume 1: Preface to Annals

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。

translations.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.

sentences.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。

translations.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.

sentences.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。

translations.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 積六十七世，至成皇帝諱毛立。

translations.literal: Accumulating sixty-seven generations, they came to Emperor Cheng, taboo name Mao, who took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After sixty-seven generations they came to Emperor Cheng, styled Mao, who was enthroned.

sentences.zh: [1]聰明武略，遠近所推，統國三十六，大姓九十九，威振北方，莫不率服。

translations.literal: [1] Intelligent and martial in strategy, esteemed near and far; he ruled thirty-six states and ninety-nine great clans, his might shaking the north, none failing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Clever and formidable in war, he was acclaimed far and near. He ruled thirty-six domains and ninety-nine great clans; his authority shook the north, and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 崩。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 節皇帝諱貸立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Jie, taboo name Dai, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jie, styled Dai, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 莊皇帝諱觀立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang, taboo name Guan, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang, styled Guan, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 明皇帝諱樓立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, taboo name Lou, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, styled Lou, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝諱越立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor An, taboo name Yue, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An, styled Yue, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 宣皇帝諱推寅立。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, taboo name Tuiyin, took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, styled Tuiyin, was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 南遷大澤，方千餘里，厥土昏冥沮洳。

translations.literal: They moved south to the Great Marsh, more than a thousand li across; its soil was dark and boggy.
translations.idiomatic: They migrated south to the Great Marsh, a domain of more than a thousand li, where the ground lay dim and sodden.

sentences.zh: 謀更南徙，未行而崩。

translations.literal: They planned to move further south but before carrying it out he died.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted to move still farther south, but before the move could be made he died.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝諱利立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Li, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, styled Li, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝諱俟立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, taboo name Qi, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, styled Qi, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 和皇帝諱肆立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor He, taboo name Si, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He, styled Si, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 定皇帝諱機立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Ding, taboo name Ji, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ding, styled Ji, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 僖皇帝諱蓋立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xi, taboo name Gai, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xi, styled Gai, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 威皇帝諱儈立，崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Wei, taboo name Kuai, took the throne. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wei, styled Kuai, was enthroned. He died.

sentences.zh: 獻皇帝諱隣立。

translations.literal: Emperor Xian, taboo name Lin, took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian, styled Lin, was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 時有神人言於國曰：「此土荒遐，未足以建都邑，宜復徙居。

translations.literal: At that time a divine being spoke in the state, saying: "This land is remote and desolate, not sufficient to establish a capital; you ought to move and settle elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Then a spirit spoke within the realm: "This country is too remote and barren to bear a capital. You should move on and settle elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 」帝時年衰老，乃以位授子。

translations.literal: " The emperor was by then old in years and so transferred the position to his son.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was by then aged and abdicated in favor of his son.

sentences.zh: 聖武皇帝諱詰汾。

translations.literal: Holy Martial Emperor, taboo name Jiefen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shengwu, styled Jiefen.

sentences.zh: 獻帝命南移，山谷高深，九難八阻，於是欲止。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor ordered a move south; the valleys were deep and the mountains high—nine hardships and eight barriers—whereupon they wished to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian had ordered them south, but the passes were steep and the ravines deep, nine perils and eight obstacles deep, and they were ready to turn back.

sentences.zh: 有神獸，其形似馬，其聲類牛，先行導引，歷年乃出。

translations.literal: There was a divine beast, shaped like a horse, its cry like an ox; it went ahead as guide, and only after years did they emerge.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit beast appeared, horse in form and lowing like an ox. It led the way, and only after many years did they break out.

sentences.zh: 始居匈奴之故地。

translations.literal: They first settled in the former territory of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: At last they made their home in the old lands of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其遷徙策略，多出宣、獻二帝，故人並號曰「推寅」，蓋俗云「鑽研」之義。

translations.literal: Most of their migration strategy came from Emperors Xuan and Xian; therefore people jointly called him "Tuiyin," roughly the sense of "to bore through and study" in common speech.
translations.idiomatic: Much of their strategy of relocation came from Emperors Xuan and Xian; people therefore nicknamed him Tuiyin—"to drill through," in the common tongue.

sentences.zh: 初，聖武帝嘗率數萬騎田於山澤，欻見輜軿自天而下。

translations.literal: Early on, Emperor Shengwu once led tens of thousands of horsemen hunting in mountains and marshes; suddenly he saw a curtained carriage descend from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Emperor Shengwu led tens of thousands of riders on a hunt through hill and fen, when suddenly a curtained carriage dropped from the sky.

sentences.zh: 既至，見美婦人，侍衞甚盛。

translations.literal: When it arrived, he saw a beautiful woman with a very grand retinue.
translations.idiomatic: When it landed, a beautiful woman stood within, attended by a great train.

sentences.zh: 帝異而問之，對曰：「我，天女也，受命相偶。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled and asked her; she replied: "I am a daughter of Heaven, ordered to be your mate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wondered and questioned her. She answered: "I am a heavenly maiden, sent to be your consort.

sentences.zh: 」遂同寢宿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they lay together.
translations.idiomatic: " That night they lay together.

sentences.zh: 旦，請還，曰：「明年周時，復會此處。

translations.literal: At dawn she asked to return, saying: "Next year at this season we shall meet again at this place.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn she asked leave to go, saying: "At this same season next year, meet me here again.

sentences.zh: 」言終而別，去如風雨。

translations.literal: " When her words were finished they parted; she left like wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: " With that she was gone, swift as wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 及期，帝至先所田處，果復相見。

translations.literal: When the season came, the emperor went to the place where he had hunted before and indeed met her again.
translations.idiomatic: When the season returned, the emperor came to the old hunting ground and found her waiting.

sentences.zh: 天女以所生男授帝曰：「此君之子也，善養視之。

translations.literal: The heavenly daughter handed the boy she had borne to the emperor, saying: "This is your lord's son; nurture and care for him well.
translations.idiomatic: The heavenly maiden placed the boy she had borne in his hands. "This is your son," she said. "Raise him with care.

sentences.zh: 子孫相承，當世為帝王。

translations.literal: " Descendants shall succeed one another and be emperors for generations.
translations.idiomatic: " His line shall rule as emperors for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 」語訖而去。

translations.literal: " When she had finished speaking she departed.
translations.idiomatic: " She spoke no more and departed.

sentences.zh: 子即始祖也。

translations.literal: The son was the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: That child was the Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故時人諺曰：「詰汾皇帝無婦家，力微皇帝無舅家。

translations.literal: Hence a popular saying of the time: "Emperor Jiefen had no wife's family; Emperor Liwei had no mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying of the age: "Emperor Jiefen had no kin by marriage; Emperor Liwei had no kin on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩。

translations.literal: " The emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor died.

sentences.zh: 始祖神元皇帝諱力微立。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor, Emperor Shenyuan, taboo name Liwei, took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor, Emperor Shenyuan, styled Liwei, was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 生而英叡。

translations.literal: From birth he was brilliant and perspicacious.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed a keen and commanding mind.

sentences.zh: 元年，歲在庚子。

translations.literal: In the first year of his reign, the year was gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: The first year of his reign fell in the gengzi year.

sentences.zh: 先是，西部內侵，國民離散，依於沒鹿回部大人竇賓。

translations.literal: Before this, the western tribes had invaded inward; the people scattered and relied on the great chief Dou Bin of the Molu Hui tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the western clans had raided inward, scattering the people, who took refuge with Dou Bin, great chief of the Molu Hui.

sentences.zh: 始祖有雄傑之度，時人莫測。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor had the measure of a hero; of the time none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor bore the stature of a hero; none of his day could read his depths.

sentences.zh: 後與賓攻西部，軍敗，失馬步走，始祖使人以所乘駿馬給之。

translations.literal: Later he and Bin attacked the western tribes; the army was defeated, Bin lost his horse and went on foot. The Founding Ancestor sent someone to give him the fine steed he himself had been riding.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Bin in an attack on the western tribes. The army was beaten; Bin lost his mount and fled on foot. The Founding Ancestor sent a man to bring him the fine horse he himself had ridden.

sentences.zh: 賓歸，令其部內求與馬之人，當加重賞，始祖隱而不言。

translations.literal: When Bin returned, he ordered those within his tribe to seek out the man who had given the horse, intending to bestow a heavy reward—but the Founding Ancestor kept silent and did not reveal himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin came home he ordered his people to find the man who had given the horse, promising a rich reward. The Founding Ancestor said nothing and would not be found.

sentences.zh: 久之，賓乃知，大驚，將分國之半，以奉始祖，始祖不受，乃進其愛女。

translations.literal: After a long time Bin finally learned of it and was greatly astonished; he was about to give half the state to serve the Founding Ancestor, but the Founding Ancestor would not accept; thereupon he presented his beloved daughter.
translations.idiomatic: In time Bin learned the truth and was astonished. He offered half his domain in homage, but the Founding Ancestor refused and would take only his beloved daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 賓猶思報恩，固問所欲。

translations.literal: Bin still wished to repay the kindness and pressed him to say what he desired.
translations.idiomatic: Bin still sought to repay the debt and pressed him: what did he wish?

sentences.zh: 始祖請率所部北居長川，賓乃敬從。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor asked to lead his own tribe to dwell north on the Long River; Bin respectfully followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor asked leave to lead his people north to the Long River, and Bin yielded with respect.

sentences.zh: 積十數歲，德化大洽，諸舊部民，咸來歸附。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, virtue and transforming influence were broadly achieved; all the old tribes came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After a dozen years his virtue had won the realm; the old tribes all came back to his banner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，賓臨終，戒其二子使謹奉始祖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as Bin lay dying, he admonished his two sons to reverently serve the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenty-ninth year, as Bin lay dying, he charged his two sons to honor and serve the Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 其子不從，乃陰謀為逆。

translations.literal: His sons did not obey and secretly plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: His sons disobeyed and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 始祖召殺之，盡并其眾，諸部大人，悉皆欵服，控弦上馬二十餘萬。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor summoned and killed them, annexing all their followers entirely; all the tribal great chiefs submitted completely—those who could string a bow and mount a horse numbered more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor had them summoned and put to death, absorbing all their followers. Every tribal chief submitted; those who could draw a bow and ride numbered more than two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，遷於定襄之盛樂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, they moved to Shengle in Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In his thirty-ninth year they moved the seat to Shengle in Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，祭天，諸部君長皆來助祭，唯白部大人觀望不至，於是徵而戮之，遠近肅然，莫不震懾。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, they sacrificed to Heaven; chiefs of all tribes came to assist in the sacrifice. Only the great chief of the White Tribe waited and did not come; thereupon he was summoned and executed. Near and far were awed; none failed to tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer they sacrificed to Heaven, and chiefs of every tribe came to join the rite. Only the White Tribe's chief held back and did not appear; he was summoned and executed. Near and far fell silent, trembling before his wrath.

sentences.zh: 始祖乃告諸大人曰：「我歷觀前世匈奴、蹋頓之徒，苟貪財利，抄掠邊民，雖有所得，而其死傷不足相補，更招寇讎，百姓塗炭，非長計也。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor then addressed the great chiefs: "I have broadly observed the Xiongnu, Tuntun and their kind of former ages—greedy for wealth and profit, raiding border peoples. Though they gained something, their dead and wounded could not make up for it; they only drew in fresh enemies, the common people smeared in charcoal—not a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor then told the chiefs: "I have watched the Xiongnu and men like Tuntun of old—greedy for plunder, harrying the borderlands. They took booty, yet their dead outweighed the gain; they only bred new enemies and left the people in ashes. That is no lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 」於是與魏和親。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they made peace marriage with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " So he made peace with Wei and sealed it by marriage.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，遣子文帝如魏，且觀風土。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he sent his son Emperor Wen to Wei, and to observe the regional customs.
translations.idiomatic: In his forty-second year he sent his son, who would be Emperor Wen, to Wei to observe its customs.

sentences.zh: 魏景元二年也。

translations.literal: It was the second year of Jingyuan of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This was the second year of Wei's Jingyuan era.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝諱沙漠汗，以國太子留洛陽，為魏賓之冠。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, taboo name Shamo Han—as the state's crown prince he remained at Luoyang, foremost among Wei's tributary guests.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, styled Shamo Han, stayed at Luoyang as the realm's crown prince—the foremost of Wei's vassal guests.

sentences.zh: 聘問交市，往來不絕，魏人奉遺金帛繒絮，歲以萬計。

translations.literal: Envoys and markets exchanged visits without cease; Wei people presented gifts of gold, silks, and floss by the tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys and merchants crossed the border without pause; each year Wei sent gold, silk, and floss in amounts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 始祖與隣國交接，篤信推誠，不為倚伏以要一時之利，寬恕任真，而遐邇歸仰。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor in dealing with neighboring states was deeply trustworthy and sincere, not using deception for momentary gain; forgiving and true to his nature, near and far came to look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: In dealings with neighboring states the Founding Ancestor was steadfast and sincere, never scheming for a moment's advantage. Forgiving and plain in nature, he won the loyalty of near and far alike.

sentences.zh: 魏晉禪代，和好仍密。

translations.literal: When Wei ceded the throne to Jin, cordial relations remained close.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei yielded the throne to Jin, the bond between them stayed close.

sentences.zh: 始祖春秋已邁，帝以父老求歸，晉武帝具禮護送。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor's years were already advanced; the emperor because the old fathers sought his return, and Emperor Wu of Jin with full rites escorted him back.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor was already old; the emperor, at his elders' plea for his return, sent him home with full ceremony under Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，帝至自晉。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, the emperor arrived from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year the prince returned from Jin.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，帝復如晉；

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, the emperor again went to Jin;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year the prince again went to Jin;

sentences.zh: 其年冬，還國。

translations.literal: that winter he returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: and that winter came home to the realm.

sentences.zh: 晉遺帝錦、罽、繒、綵、綿、絹、諸物，咸出豐厚，車牛百乘。

translations.literal: Jin presented the emperor brocade, felt, silk, colored silks, cotton, gauze—all manner of goods, lavishly generous, a hundred cartloads of cattle and oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent him brocade, felt, silk, dyed cloth, cotton, gauze—gifts in lavish profusion, and a hundred ox-carts besides.

sentences.zh: 行達并州，晉征北將軍衞瓘，以帝為人雄異，恐為後患，乃密啟晉帝，請留不遣。

translations.literal: When the journey reached Bingzhou, Jin's General Who Conquers the North Wei Guan, because the emperor was a man of heroic singularity, feared he would be a later trouble—thereupon secretly memorialized the Jin emperor requesting to detain him and not send him on.
translations.idiomatic: At Bingzhou, Jin's northern commander Wei Guan saw in the prince a man of singular power and feared trouble later on. He secretly memorialized the Jin throne to hold him and not let him go.

sentences.zh: 晉帝難於失信，不許。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor found it hard to break faith and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor would not break his word and refused.

sentences.zh: 瓘復請以金錦賂國之大人，令致間隙，使相危害。

translations.literal: Wei Guan again requested to use gold and brocade to bribe the state's great chiefs, causing them to sow discord so that they would harm one another.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan asked again to buy off the realm's chiefs with gold and brocade, sowing discord so they would turn on one another.

sentences.zh: 晉帝從之，遂留帝。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor assented and thus detained the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor agreed, and so the prince was kept.

sentences.zh: 於是國之執事及外部大人，皆受瓘貨。

translations.literal: Thereupon the state's executives and the outer great chiefs all received Wei Guan's bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court officers and the outer chiefs all took Wei Guan's gifts.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，方遣帝。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, they finally sent the emperor off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year they at last let the prince go.

sentences.zh: 始祖聞帝歸，大悅，使諸部大人詣陰館迎之。

translations.literal: When the Founding Ancestor heard the emperor was returning he was greatly pleased and sent great chiefs of various tribes to Yin Lodge to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Ancestor learned the prince was coming home he rejoiced and sent chiefs of every tribe to Yin Lodge to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，帝仰視飛鳥，謂諸大人曰：「我為汝曹取之。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, the emperor looked up at birds in flight and said to the great chiefs: "I will take them for you all.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine deepened, the prince looked up at birds on the wing and told the chiefs: "I will fetch those down for you.

sentences.zh: 」援彈飛丸，應弦而落。

translations.literal: He took up his pellet-bow and flying pellets; at the twang of the string they fell.
translations.idiomatic: He took up a pellet bow and shot; at the snap of the string the birds dropped.

sentences.zh: 時國俗無彈，眾咸大驚，乃相謂曰：「太子風彩被服，同於南夏，兼奇術絕世，若繼國統，變易舊俗，吾等必不得志，不若在國諸子，習本淳樸。

translations.literal: At that time the state custom had no pellet-bows; the multitude was greatly startled and said among themselves: "The crown prince's manner and dress are like those of Southern Xia, and his strange arts surpass the world—if he inherits the state succession and alters the old customs, we shall certainly not get our way; better the sons within the state, who are versed in our native simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had never known the pellet bow; all were astonished and whispered: "The crown prince dresses and carries himself like the southern Chinese, and his uncanny skill has no match. If he inherits the throne and changes our ways, we shall lose our standing. Better a son raised here, steeped in our old simplicity.

sentences.zh: 」咸以為然。

translations.literal: " All thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: " They were agreed.

sentences.zh: 且離間素行，乃謀危害，並先馳還。

translations.literal: Moreover the discord sown for many years—thereupon they plotted harm, and all galloped ahead to return first.
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of division Wei Guan had planted were already ripe; they plotted against the prince and raced home ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 始祖問曰：「我子既歷他國，進德何如？

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor asked: "My son, having passed through another state—how has his virtue advanced?
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor asked: "My son has lived in a foreign land—how has his character grown?

sentences.zh: 」皆對曰：「太子才藝非常，引空弓而落飛鳥，是似得晉人異法怪術，亂國害民之兆，惟願察之。

translations.literal: " All replied: "The crown prince's talent is extraordinary; drawing an empty bow he brought down a flying bird—that is as if he had obtained Jin men's strange methods and occult arts, a portent of disordering the state and harming the people. We wish Your Majesty would examine this.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered: "The crown prince's gifts are beyond the common run. He drew an empty bow and felled a bird in flight—as if he had learned Jin sorcery. It is an omen of chaos and harm to the people. We beg Your Majesty to look into this.

sentences.zh: 」自帝在晉之後，諸子愛寵日進，始祖年踰期頤，頗有所惑，聞諸大人之語，意乃有疑。

translations.literal: From the time the prince had been in Jin, the love and favor toward the other sons daily grew; the Founding Ancestor, more than a hundred years old, was somewhat confused; hearing the great chiefs' words, his mind came to harbor doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Since the prince had gone to Jin, the other sons had won favor day by day. The Founding Ancestor was past a hundred and his mind was clouded; hearing the chiefs, he began to doubt.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「不可容者，便當除之。

translations.literal: He said: "Whoever cannot be tolerated—just remove him.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "If he cannot be borne, then do away with him.

sentences.zh: 」於是諸大人乃馳詣塞南，矯害帝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the great chiefs galloped to the south of the passes and, by forged command, killed the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " The chiefs galloped south of the frontier passes and, by forged order, killed the prince.

sentences.zh: 既而，始祖甚悔之。

translations.literal: Before long the Founding Ancestor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Founding Ancestor was filled with remorse.

sentences.zh: 帝身長八尺，英姿瓌偉，在晉之日，朝士英俊多與親善，雅為人物歸仰。

translations.literal: The emperor stood eight feet in height, heroic and magnificent in bearing; during his days in Jin many of the court's gifted men were fond of him—he was esteemed among men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The prince stood eight feet tall, splendid in bearing. In Jin many of the court's finest men befriended him; men of the age looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 後乃追諡焉。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed with a title.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was given a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 章皇帝諱悉鹿立，始祖之子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang, taboo name Silu, took the throne—son of the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang, styled Silu, was enthroned—son of the Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 諸部離叛，國內紛擾。

translations.literal: The tribes drifted apart in rebellion; within the state there was turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes broke away in revolt; the realm fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 饗國九年而崩。

translations.literal: He ruled the state nine years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned nine years and died.

sentences.zh: 平皇帝諱綽立，章帝之少弟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ping, taboo name Chuo, took the throne—younger brother of Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ping, styled Chuo, was enthroned—younger brother of Emperor Zhang.

sentences.zh: 雄武有智略，威德復舉。

translations.literal: Bold in war with wisdom and stratagem; prestige and virtue rose again.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce in battle and shrewd in counsel; prestige and virtue were restored.

sentences.zh: 七年，匈奴宇文部大人莫槐為其下所殺，更立莫槐弟普撥為大人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Mo Huai, great chief of the Xiongnu Yuwen tribe, was killed by his subordinates; they established Mo Huai's younger brother Puba as great chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Mo Huai, great chief of the Yuwen Xiongnu, was slain by his own men, who set up his younger brother Puba in his place.

sentences.zh: 帝以女妻撥子丘不懃。

translations.literal: The emperor gave his daughter in marriage to Puba's son Qiubuqin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave his daughter to Puba's son Qiubuqin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝饗國七年而崩。

translations.literal: The emperor ruled the state seven years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned seven years and died.

sentences.zh: 思皇帝諱弗立，文帝之少子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Si, taboo name Fu, took the throne—younger son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si, styled Fu, was enthroned—younger son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 聰哲有大度，為諸父兄所重。

translations.literal: Intelligent and wise with great magnanimity; he was esteemed by his uncles and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, far-sighted, and magnanimous, he was held in honor by his uncles and elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 政崇寬簡，百姓懷服。

translations.literal: His government honored leniency and simplicity; the common people embraced and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and ease, and the people gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 饗國一年而崩。

translations.literal: He ruled the state one year and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned one year and died.

sentences.zh: 昭皇帝諱祿官立，始祖之子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao, taboo name Luoguan, took the throne—son of the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhao, styled Luoguan, was enthroned—son of the Founding Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 分國為三部：帝自以一部居東，在上谷北，濡源之西，東接宇文部；

translations.literal: He divided the state into three parts: the emperor himself kept one part in the east, north of Shanggu, west of the Ru source, bordering the Yuwen tribe to the east;
translations.idiomatic: He split the realm into three domains: the emperor kept the eastern third himself, north of Shanggu and west of the Ru River, with the Yuwen tribe on his eastern flank;

sentences.zh: 以文帝之長子桓皇帝諱猗㐌統一部，居代郡之參合陂北；

translations.literal: he assigned the eldest son of Emperor Wen, Emperor Huan, taboo name Yiyi, to lead one part, dwelling north of Canhepo in Dai commandery;
translations.idiomatic: he gave Emperor Wen's eldest son, Emperor Huan, styled Yiyi, one third, with his seat north of Canhe Marsh in Dai commandery;

sentences.zh: 以桓帝之弟穆皇帝諱猗盧統一部，居定襄之盛樂故城。

translations.literal: he assigned Emperor Huan's younger brother Emperor Mu, taboo name Yilu, to lead one part, dwelling at the old city of Shengle in Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: and he gave Emperor Huan's younger brother, Emperor Mu, styled Yilu, the third, based at the old capital of Shengle in Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 自始祖以來，與晉和好，百姓乂安，財畜富實，控弦騎士四十餘萬。

translations.literal: From the Founding Ancestor onward they had been at peace with Jin; the people were secure, wealth and livestock abundant, with more than four hundred thousand mounted archers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Founding Ancestor's day they had lived at peace with Jin; the people prospered, herds and stores were full, and they could field more than four hundred thousand horse archers.

sentences.zh: 是歲，穆帝始出并州，遷雜胡北徙雲中、五原、朔方。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Mu first left Bing province, moving various Hu peoples north to Yunzhong, Wuyuan, and Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Mu marched out of Bing province and resettled mixed non-Han peoples north into Yunzhong, Wuyuan, and Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 又西渡河擊匈奴、烏桓諸部。

translations.literal: He also crossed the river westward to attack the Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He also crossed the Yellow River west to strike the Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 自杏城以北八十里，迄長城原，夾道立碣，與晉分界。

translations.literal: From eighty li north of Xingcheng to the Great Wall plain, boundary stones were set along the road to mark the border with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: From eighty li north of Xingcheng to the edge of the Great Wall, they set up boundary markers along the road to divide their land from Jin.

sentences.zh: 二年，葬文帝及皇后封氏。

translations.literal: In the second year they buried Emperor Wen and Empress Lady Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they interred Emperor Wen and Empress Feng.

sentences.zh: 初，思帝欲改葬，未果而崩。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Si had wished to rebury them, but before accomplishing it he died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Si had planned a reburial, but died before it could be done.

sentences.zh: 至是，述成前意焉。

translations.literal: Now they fulfilled his earlier intention.
translations.idiomatic: At last they carried out what he had intended.

sentences.zh: 晉成都王司馬穎遣從事中郎田思，河間王司馬顒遣司馬靳利，并州刺史司馬騰遣主簿梁天，並來會葬。

translations.literal: Sima Ying the Prince of Chengdu sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Tian Si; Sima Yong the Prince of Hejian sent Commandant Jin Li; Sima Teng the Inspector of Bingzhou sent Registrar Liang Tian—all came for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, sent Tian Si as attendant-in-ordinary; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, sent Commandant Jin Li; Sima Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, sent registrar Liang Tian—all to attend the burial.

sentences.zh: 遠近赴者二十萬人。

translations.literal: From near and far two hundred thousand came to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly two hundred thousand mourners came from near and far.

sentences.zh: 三年，[2]桓帝度漠北巡，因西略諸國。

translations.literal: In the third year [2] Emperor Huan crossed the desert on a northern tour and thereupon campaigned west against the various states.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year [2] Emperor Huan crossed the northern desert on campaign and turned west to subdue the western states.

sentences.zh: 四年，東部未耐婁大人倍斤入居遼東。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Beinarou the great chief of the eastern Weinü entered and settled in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Beinarou, great chief of the eastern Weinü, moved into Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 五年，宇文莫廆之子遜昵延朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Xunniyan, son of Yuwen Mohuang, came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Xunniyan, son of Yuwen Mohuang, presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其誠欵，以長女妻焉。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his sincerity and gave his eldest daughter in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his good faith and gave him his eldest daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 七年，桓帝至自西略，諸降附者二十餘國，凡積五歲，今始東還。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Emperor Huan returned from the western campaign; more than twenty states had submitted—in all five years, and now he came back east.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Emperor Huan returned from the west; more than twenty states had submitted to him. Five years had passed, and at last he turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉惠帝為成都王穎逼留在鄴。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Emperor Hui of Jin was compelled by Sima Ying the Prince of Chengdu to remain at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Emperor Hui of Jin was held at Ye by Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 匈奴別種劉淵反於離石，自號漢王。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan, a separate branch of the Xiongnu, rebelled at Lishi and styled himself King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, of a Xiongnu splinter line, rose at Lishi and proclaimed himself King of Han.

sentences.zh: 并州刺史司馬騰來乞師，桓帝率十餘萬騎，帝亦同時大舉以助之，大破淵眾於西河、上黨。

translations.literal: Sima Teng, Inspector of Bingzhou, came to beg troops; Emperor Huan led more than a hundred thousand horse, and the emperor also launched a great campaign at the same time to assist, thoroughly defeating Liu Yuan's host at Xihe and Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, begged for aid. Emperor Huan led more than a hundred thousand cavalry, and Emperor Zhao mobilized on the same scale; together they shattered Liu Yuan's forces at Xihe and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 會惠帝還洛，騰乃辭師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, Teng then dismissed the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui was restored to Luoyang, Teng released the allied troops.

sentences.zh: 桓帝與騰盟於汾東而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan made alliance with Teng east of the Fen and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan swore alliance with Teng east of the Fen River and marched home.

sentences.zh: 乃使輔相衞雄、段繁，於參合陂西累石為亭，樹碑以記行焉。

translations.literal: He sent his aides Wei Xiong and Duan Fan west of Canhepo to pile stones into a pavilion and set up a stele to record the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He had his ministers Wei Xiong and Duan Fan raise a stone pavilion west of Canhe Marsh and erect a stele to commemorate the campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一年，劉淵攻司馬騰，騰復乞師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Liu Yuan attacked Sima Teng; Teng again begged troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Liu Yuan attacked Sima Teng, who again begged for troops.

sentences.zh: 桓帝以輕騎數千救之，斬淵將綦毋豚，淵南走蒲子。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan with several thousand light horse came to the rescue, beheaded Liu Yuan's general Qimu Tun, and Yuan fled south to Puzi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan rode to the rescue with a few thousand light cavalry, slew Liu Yuan's general Qimu Tun, and Yuan fled south to Puzi.

sentences.zh: 晉假桓帝大單于，金印紫綬。

translations.literal: Jin enfeoffed Emperor Huan as Great Chanyu with a golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: Jin invested Emperor Huan as Great Chanyu, granting a golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 是歲，桓帝崩。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Huan died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Huan died.

sentences.zh: 帝英傑魁岸，馬不能勝。

translations.literal: The emperor was outstandingly heroic and of towering stature; horses could not bear his weight.
translations.idiomatic: He was a heroic, towering figure—ordinary horses could not carry him.

sentences.zh: 常乘安車，駕大牛，牛角容一石。

translations.literal: He commonly rode in a secure carriage drawn by great oxen; the ox horns could hold a dan of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He usually traveled in a secure cart pulled by huge oxen whose horns could hold a full stone of grain.

sentences.zh: 帝曾中蠱，嘔吐之地仍生榆木。

translations.literal: The emperor was once poisoned by gu; where he vomited an elm tree grew.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after he had been poisoned, an elm tree sprang up where he had vomited.

sentences.zh: 參合陂土無榆樹，故世人異之，至今傳記。

translations.literal: There were no elm trees on the soil of Canhepo, so people considered it strange, and it is recorded to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Canhe Marsh had no elms in its soil, so people marveled at it—a wonder still told in chronicles.

sentences.zh: 帝統部凡十一年。

translations.literal: The emperor ruled his part for eleven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In all he ruled his domain eleven years.

sentences.zh: 後定襄侯衞操，樹碑於大邗城，以頌功德。

translations.literal: Later Wei Chao, Marquis of Dingxiang, set up a stele at Dagancheng to extol his merits.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Chao, marquis of Dingxiang, raised a stele at Dagancheng praising his achievements.

sentences.zh: 子普根代立。

translations.literal: His son Pugen succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pugen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，賨人李雄，僭帝號於蜀，自稱大成。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Li Xiong of the Ba people usurped an imperial title in Shu, styling his state Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Li Xiong of the Ba seized an imperial title in Shu and called his realm Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 十三年，昭帝崩。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Emperor Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Emperor Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 徒何大單于慕容廆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Murong Hui the Great Chanyu of the Tuohe sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui, Great Chanyu of the Tuohe, sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，羯胡石勒與晉馬牧帥汲桑反。

translations.literal: That year the Jie barbarian Shi Le and Ji Sang, director of Jin's horse pastures, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Jie chieftain Shi Le and Ji Sang, overseer of Jin's stud farms, rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 穆皇帝天姿英特，勇略過人，昭帝崩後，遂總攝三部，以為一統。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu was naturally outstanding and brave beyond others; after Emperor Zhao died he took overall charge of the three parts and unified them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu was born extraordinary, his courage and stratagem surpassing other men. After Emperor Zhao's death he gathered the three domains into one rule.

sentences.zh: 元年，劉淵僭帝號，自稱大漢。

translations.literal: In the first year Liu Yuan usurped an imperial title, styling himself Great Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year Liu Yuan took the imperial title and called his state Great Han.

sentences.zh: 三年，晉并州刺史劉琨遣使，以子遵為質。

translations.literal: In the third year Liu Kun the Inspector of Bingzhou sent envoys, offering his son Zun as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Kun, inspector of Bingzhou, sent envoys and offered his son Zun as hostage.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，厚報饋之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his intent and richly rewarded and returned the gift.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his loyalty and sent back lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 白部大人叛入西河，鐵弗劉虎舉眾於雁門以應之，攻琨新興、雁門二郡。

translations.literal: The great chief of the Bai tribe rebelled and entered Xihe; Tiefo Liu Hu raised hosts at Yanmen in response, attacking Kun's Xinxing and Yanmen commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai chieftain rebelled into Xihe; Liu Hu of the Tiefo Xiongnu mustered troops at Yanmen to join him and struck Kun's Xinxing and Yanmen commanderies.

sentences.zh: 琨來乞師，帝使弟子平文皇帝將騎二萬，助琨擊之，大破白部；

translations.literal: Kun came to beg troops; the emperor sent his nephew Emperor Pingwen at the head of twenty thousand horse to assist Kun in attacking; they thoroughly defeated the Bai tribe;
translations.idiomatic: Kun begged for troops. The emperor sent his nephew, who would become Emperor Pingwen, with twenty thousand cavalry to aid him. They routed the Bai;

sentences.zh: 次攻劉虎，屠其營落。

translations.literal: next they attacked Liu Hu and slaughtered his encampments.
translations.idiomatic: then turned on Liu Hu and destroyed his camps.

sentences.zh: 虎收其餘燼，西走度河，竄居朔方。

translations.literal: Hu gathered the remainder and fled west across the river, hiding in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu gathered what was left, fled west across the river, and hid in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝進帝大單于，封代公。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin advanced the emperor to Great Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai of Jin promoted him to Great Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 帝以封邑去國懸遠，民不相接，乃從琨求句注陘北之地。

translations.literal: Because the enfeoffment was far from the state and the people were not contiguous, he asked Kun for the lands north of Gouzhu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His fief lay too far from the heartland and did not adjoin his people, so he asked Kun for the territory north of Gouzhu Pass.

sentences.zh: 琨自以託附，聞之大喜，乃徙馬邑、陰館、樓煩、繁畤、崞五縣之民於陘南，更立城邑，盡獻其地，東接代郡，西連西河、朔方，[3]方數百里。

translations.literal: Kun, relying on this attachment, was greatly pleased; he moved the people of Mayi, Yin'an, Loufan, Fanzhi, and Guo five counties south of the pass, reestablished cities and towns, and ceded all the land entirely—east adjoining Dai commandery, west connecting Xihe and Shuofang, [3] several hundred li square.
translations.idiomatic: Kun, glad to have such an ally, resettled the people of Mayi, Yin'an, Loufan, Fanzhi, and Guo—the five counties—south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and yielded the whole region: east to Dai commandery, west to Xihe and Shuofang, [3] a domain hundreds of li across.

sentences.zh: 帝乃徙十萬家以充之。

translations.literal: The emperor then moved one hundred thousand households to populate it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then relocated a hundred thousand families to fill the new lands.

sentences.zh: 劉琨又遣使乞師救洛陽，帝遣步騎二萬助之，晉太傅東海王司馬越辭以洛中飢饉，師乃還。

translations.literal: Liu Kun again sent envoys begging troops to save Luoyang; the emperor sent twenty thousand foot and horse to assist; Sima Yue the Grand Tutor and Prince of Donghai declined on grounds of famine in Luoyang, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun again begged troops to relieve Luoyang. The emperor sent twenty thousand infantry and cavalry, but Sima Yue, grand tutor and Prince of Donghai, pleaded famine in the capital and the force turned back.

sentences.zh: 是年，劉淵死，子聰僭立。

translations.literal: That year Liu Yuan died; his son Cong usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Yuan died and his son Cong seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 四年，劉琨牙門將邢延據新興叛，[4]招引劉聰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xing Yan, gate officer of Liu Kun, seized Xinxing in rebellion, [4] drawing in Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Xing Yan, Liu Kun's gate officer, rebelled and held Xinxing, [4] calling in Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 帝遣軍討之，聰退走。

translations.literal: The emperor sent troops to attack; Cong retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent troops against him; Cong withdrew in flight.

sentences.zh: 五年，劉琨遣使乞師以討劉聰、石勒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Liu Kun sent envoys begging troops to attack Liu Cong and Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Liu Kun sent envoys begging troops to strike Liu Cong and Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 帝以琨忠義，矜而許之。

translations.literal: Because Kun was loyal and righteous, the emperor took pity and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for Kun's loyalty, the emperor pitied him and agreed.

sentences.zh: 會聰遣其子粲襲晉陽，害琨父母而據其城，琨來告難，帝大怒，遣長子六脩、桓帝子普根，及衞雄、范班、姬澹等為前鋒，帝躬統大眾二十萬為後繼。

translations.literal: When Cong sent his son Can to raid Jinyang, killing Kun's parents and seizing the city, Kun came to report the disaster; the emperor was greatly angered and sent his eldest son Liuxiu, Pugen son of Emperor Huan, and Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, Ji Dan and others as vanguard, while the emperor himself commanded a great host of two hundred thousand as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong's son Can stormed Jinyang, killed Kun's parents, and took the city, Kun came with the news. The emperor was furious. He sent his eldest son Liuxiu, Emperor Huan's son Pugen, and Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, Ji Dan, and others in the van, while he himself followed with two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 粲懼，焚輜重，突圍遁走。

translations.literal: Can was afraid, burned baggage, and broke through to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Can panicked, burned his supply train, and broke out in flight.

sentences.zh: 縱騎追之，斬其將劉儒、劉豐、簡令、張平、邢延，伏尸數百里。

translations.literal: They loosed horse in pursuit, beheading his generals Liu Ru, Liu Feng, Jian Ling, Zhang Ping, and Xing Yan; corpses lay for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing cavalry cut down his generals Liu Ru, Liu Feng, Jian Ling, Zhang Ping, and Xing Yan; the dead stretched for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 琨來拜謝，帝以禮待之。

translations.literal: Kun came to pay respects in thanks; the emperor treated him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Kun came to give thanks; the emperor received him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 琨固請進軍，帝曰：「吾不早來，致卿父母見害，誠以相愧。

translations.literal: Kun strongly urged advance; the emperor said: "Had I not come earlier, causing your parents to be killed, I would truly be ashamed before you.
translations.idiomatic: Kun pressed him to march on. The emperor said, "If I had not come late—if your parents had not died on my account—I would be ashamed indeed.

sentences.zh: 今卿已復州境，然吾遠來，士馬疲弊，且待終舉。

translations.literal: Now you have recovered your prefecture; yet I came from afar, and men and horses are weary—wait until the final campaign.
translations.idiomatic: You have won back your province, but my men and horses are spent after the long march. Wait until we strike the final blow.

sentences.zh: 賊奚可盡乎？

translations.literal: Can the enemy be exterminated entirely?"
translations.idiomatic: Can every foe be wiped out at once?"

sentences.zh: 」饋琨馬牛羊各千餘，車令百乘，[5]又留勁銳戍之而還。

translations.literal: He gave Kun more than a thousand each of horses, cattle, and sheep, a hundred chariots of orders, [5] and left elite troops to garrison before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He presented Kun with more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep apiece, a hundred wagons of provisions, [5] left picked troops to garrison the city, and withdrew.

translations.literal: Source annotation [6].
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note [6].

sentences.zh: 是年，晉雍州刺史賈疋、京兆太守閻鼎，以晉懷帝為劉聰所執，共立懷帝兄子秦王業為太子，於長安稱行臺。

translations.literal: That year Jia Pi, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Yan Ding, Defender of Jingzhao, because Emperor Huai had been seized by Liu Cong, together enthroned the Prince of Qin Ye, elder brother's son of Emperor Huai, as heir apparent at Chang'an under the title of Provisional Government.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jia Pi, inspector of Yongzhou, and Yan Ding, defender of Jingzhao—because Emperor Huai was Liu Cong's prisoner—set up Emperor Huai's nephew, Prince Ye of Qin, as heir apparent at Chang'an under a provisional regime.

sentences.zh: 帝復戒嚴，與琨更剋大舉。

translations.literal: The emperor again instituted martial law and made a new appointment with Kun for a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again mobilized for war and fixed a new date with Kun for a joint offensive.

sentences.zh: 命琨自列晉行臺，部分諸軍，帝將遣十萬騎從西河鑒谷南出，晉軍從蒲坂東度，會於平陽，就食聰粟，迎復晉帝。

translations.literal: He ordered Kun himself to erect the Jin provisional government and divide the forces; the emperor would send a hundred thousand horse south from Jian'gu Valley west of Xihe, Jin's army east from Puban Ford, meeting at Pingyang, living on Cong's grain, to welcome and restore the Jin emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was to proclaim the Jin provisional government and array his forces. The emperor would lead a hundred thousand cavalry south through Jian'gu west of Xihe; Jin's army would cross east from Puban. They would meet at Pingyang, feed on Cong's grain, and restore the Jin emperor.

sentences.zh: 事不果行。

translations.literal: The plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 六年，城盛樂以為北都，修故平城以為南都。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they walled Shengle as the northern capital and repaired old Pingcheng as the southern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they fortified Shengle as the northern capital and restored old Pingcheng as the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 帝登平城西山，觀望地勢，乃更南百里，於灅水之陽黃瓜堆築新平城，晉人謂之小平城，使長子六脩鎮之，統領南部。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the western hills of Pingcheng to survey the terrain; then a hundred li farther south on the south bank of the Sui River at Huangguadui they built New Pingcheng—Jin people called it Little Pingcheng—and stationed his eldest son Liuxiu there to command the southern part.
translations.idiomatic: From the western heights of Pingcheng he studied the land, then moved a hundred li south to Huangguadui on the south bank of the Sui River and built New Pingcheng—Chinese called it Little Pingcheng—placing his eldest son Liuxiu there to govern the south.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝復與劉琨約期，會於平陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor again made an appointment with Liu Kun to meet at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he again fixed a rendezvous with Liu Kun at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 會石勒擒王浚，國有匈奴雜胡萬餘家，多勒種類，聞勒破幽州，乃謀為亂，欲以應勒，發覺，伏誅，討聰之計，於是中止。

translations.literal: When Shi Le captured Wang Jun, within the state there were more than ten thousand households of mixed Xiongnu Hu, many of Le's kind; hearing Le had taken Youzhou, they plotted rebellion to respond to Le; discovered, they were executed; the plan to attack Cong was thereby halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le took Wang Jun, more than ten thousand Xiongnu and other Hu households within the realm—many of them Le's kin—heard he had seized Youzhou and plotted revolt in his favor. The plot was uncovered and the ringleaders executed; the campaign against Cong was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 八年，晉愍帝進帝為代王，置官屬，食代、常山二郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Emperor Min of Jin advanced the emperor to King of Dai, established officials, with revenue from Dai and Changshan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Emperor Min of Jin raised him to King of Dai, gave him a full court, and granted the revenues of Dai and Changshan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 帝忿聰、勒之亂，志欲平之。

translations.literal: The emperor resented the disorder of Cong and Le and was determined to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He burned with anger at Cong and Le and meant to crush them.

sentences.zh: 先是，國俗寬簡，民未知禁。

translations.literal: Earlier the national custom had been lenient and simple; the people did not yet know prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the nation's ways had been easy and plain; the people scarcely knew law.

sentences.zh: 至是，明刑峻法，諸部民多以違命得罪。

translations.literal: Now bright punishments and severe laws—among the tribes many offended by disobeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: Now he proclaimed stern statutes, and across the tribes many fell afoul of his commands.

sentences.zh: 凡後期者皆舉部戮之，或有室家相攜而赴死所，人問「何之」，答曰「當往就誅」。

translations.literal: All who were late were punished by slaughter of the entire tribe; some families went together to the place of execution; asked "where are you going" they answered "we are going to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone late to muster saw his whole tribe put to death. Whole households walked together to the killing ground; when asked, "Where are you going?" they answered, "To be put to death."

sentences.zh: 其威嚴伏物，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His awesomeness subdued things—all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the awe in which he held men and things.

sentences.zh: 平文皇帝諱鬱律立，思帝之子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Pingwen, taboo name Yulü, took the throne—son of Emperor Si.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen, styled Yulü, was enthroned—son of Emperor Si.

sentences.zh: 姿質雄壯，甚有威略。

translations.literal: Striking in bearing, powerfully built, with great martial prestige and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in stature, mighty in frame, and masterful in war and counsel.

sentences.zh: 元年，歲在丁丑。

translations.literal: In the first year the year was in dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: The first year was dingchou.

sentences.zh: 二年，劉虎據朔方，來侵西部，帝逆擊，大破之，虎單騎迸走。

translations.literal: In the second year Liu Hu held Shuofang and came to invade the western part; the emperor met him in attack and thoroughly defeated him; Hu fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Liu Hu, entrenched in Shuofang, invaded the west. The emperor met him and routed him; Hu escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 其從弟路孤率部落內附，帝以女妻之。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Lugu led his tribe to submit inward; the emperor gave his daughter in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Lugu brought his people in submission; the emperor gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 西兼烏孫故地，東吞勿吉以西，控弦上馬將有百萬。

translations.literal: Westward he absorbed the old lands of Wusun; eastward he swallowed west of Wuji; those who could draw bow and mount horse approached a million.
translations.idiomatic: He absorbed the old Wusun lands in the west and seized the country west of Wuji in the east; bowmen and horsemen neared a million.

sentences.zh: 劉聰死，子粲僭立，為其將靳準所殺，淵族子曜僭立。

translations.literal: Liu Cong died; his son Can usurped the throne and was killed by his general Jin Zhun; Liu Yuan's clansman Yao usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong died. His son Can seized the throne but was slain by his general Jin Zhun; Liu Yuan's kinsman Yao then took power.

sentences.zh: 帝聞晉愍帝為曜所害，顧謂大臣曰：「今中原無主，天其資我乎？

translations.literal: Hearing Emperor Min of Jin had been killed by Yao, he turned to his ministers and said: "Now the Central Plains have no lord—is Heaven perhaps endowing us?"
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Emperor Min of Jin had been killed by Yao, he said to his ministers, "The heartland is masterless. Does Heaven mean to bless us?"

sentences.zh: 」劉曜遣使請和，帝不納。

translations.literal: Liu Yao sent envoys seeking peace; the emperor would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent envoys suing for peace; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是年，司馬叡僭稱大位於江南。

translations.literal: That year Sima Rui usurped the great position in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Rui seized the imperial seat south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 三年，石勒自稱趙王，遣使乞和，請為兄弟。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi Le styled himself King of Zhao, sent envoys begging peace, asking to become brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi Le declared himself King of Zhao and sent envoys seeking peace, proposing brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 帝斬其使以絕之。

translations.literal: The emperor beheaded his envoys to break off relations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the envoys beheaded and broke off relations.

sentences.zh: 四年，私署涼州刺史張茂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhang Mao who had privately appointed himself Governor of Liangzhou sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhang Mao, who had taken the title of governor of Liangzhou on his own authority, sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，僭晉司馬叡，遣使韓暢加崇爵服，帝絕之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the usurper Jin Sima Rui sent the envoy Han Chang to add lofty rank and regalia; the emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Jin usurper Sima Rui sent Han Chang to offer elevated rank and robes of honor; the emperor rejected them.

sentences.zh: 治兵講武，有平南夏之意。

translations.literal: He drilled troops and reviewed arms, with intent to pacify southern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his armies and sharpened his weapons, intending to conquer the southern lands.

sentences.zh: 桓帝后以帝得眾心，恐不利於己子，害帝，遂崩，大人死者數十人。

translations.literal: The empress after Emperor Huan, fearing the emperor had won the people's hearts and that it would harm her own son, killed the emperor; he died—several tens of great ladies perished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan's widow, fearing that his hold on the people's loyalty would endanger her son, had the emperor murdered. Dozens of high-ranking women died with him.

sentences.zh: 天興初，尊曰太祖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing he was honored as Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianxing era began, he was posthumously titled Taizu.

sentences.zh: 惠皇帝諱賀傉立，桓帝之中子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui, taboo name Heluo, succeeded to the throne; he was the middle son of Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui, whose taboo name was Heluo, came to the throne; he was Emperor Huan's second son.

sentences.zh: 以五年為元年。

translations.literal: The fifth year was taken as the first year of his reign.
translations.idiomatic: He took the fifth year as the first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 未親政事，太后臨朝，遣使與石勒通和，時人謂之女國使。

translations.literal: He did not personally attend to government; the empress dowager held court, sent envoys to make peace with Shi Le—people of the time called this the "women's-state embassy."
translations.idiomatic: He did not yet govern in person. The empress dowager held court and sent envoys to treat with Shi Le; contemporaries called them the "women's-state envoys."

sentences.zh: 二年，司馬叡死，子紹僭立。

translations.literal: In the second year Sima Rui died; his son Shao usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Sima Rui died, and his son Shao usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝始臨朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor began to hold court himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor at last took the throne in person.

sentences.zh: 以諸部人情未悉欵順，乃築城於東木根山，徙都之。

translations.literal: Because the hearts of the various tribes were not yet fully loyal and submissive, they built a city at Eastern Mugen Mountain and moved the capital there.
translations.idiomatic: Because the tribes had not yet fully submitted in good faith, a city was built on Eastern Mugen Mountain and the capital was moved there.

sentences.zh: 是年，張茂死，兄寔子駿立，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Mao died; his elder brother Shi's son Jun succeeded and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Mao died. His elder brother Shi's son Jun succeeded and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 是年，司馬紹死，子衍僭立。

translations.literal: That year Sima Shao died; his son Yan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Shao died, and his son Yan usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 煬皇帝諱紇那立，惠帝之弟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang, taboo name Hena, succeeded; he was younger brother of Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang, taboo name Hena, took the throne; he was Emperor Hui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 以五年為元年。

translations.literal: The fifth year was taken as the first year of his reign.
translations.idiomatic: He took the fifth year as the first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 三年，石勒遣石虎率騎五千來寇邊部，帝禦之於句注陘北，不利，遷於大寧。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi Le sent Shi Hu leading five thousand horse to raid the border territories; the emperor confronted them north of Gouzhu Pass, fared poorly, and moved to Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi Le sent Shi Hu at the head of five thousand cavalry to raid the borderlands. The emperor met them north of Gouzhu Pass, was defeated, and withdrew to Daning.

sentences.zh: 時烈帝居於舅賀蘭部，帝遣使求之，賀蘭部帥藹頭，擁護不遣。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Lie was dwelling with his maternal uncle's Helan tribe; the emperor sent envoys to request him back; the Helan chieftain Aitou protected him and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Lie was living with his maternal uncle's Helan tribe. The emperor sent envoys to fetch him, but the Helan chieftain Aitou shielded him and refused to let him go.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召宇文部并勢擊藹頭。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned the Yuwen tribe and combined forces to attack Aitou.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor called up the Yuwen tribe and joined forces to strike Aitou.

sentences.zh: 宇文眾敗，帝還大寧。

translations.literal: The Yuwen forces were defeated; the emperor returned to Daning.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen army was beaten, and the emperor returned to Daning.

sentences.zh: 四年，石勒擒劉曜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Shi Le captured Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Shi Le captured Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝出居於宇文部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor went out and dwelt with the Yuwen tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor went out and took up residence with the Yuwen tribe.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭及諸部大人，共立烈帝。

translations.literal: Helan and the great ladies of the various tribes jointly installed Emperor Lie.
translations.idiomatic: The Helan and the great ladies of the tribes together enthroned Emperor Lie.

sentences.zh: 烈皇帝諱翳槐立，平文之長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Lie, taboo name Yihua, succeeded; he was the eldest son of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lie, taboo name Yihua, succeeded; he was the eldest son of Emperor Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 以五年為元年。

translations.literal: The fifth year was taken as the first year of his reign.
translations.idiomatic: He took the fifth year as the first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣使求和，帝遣弟昭成皇帝如襄國，從者五千餘家。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent envoys seeking peace; the emperor sent his younger brother, who would become Emperor Zhaocheng, to Xiangguo, with more than five thousand households following.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent envoys suing for peace. The emperor sent his younger brother—the future Emperor Zhaocheng—to Xiangguo, followed by more than five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二年，石勒僭立，自稱大趙王。

translations.literal: In the second year Shi Le usurped the throne and styled himself Great King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Shi Le usurped power and styled himself Great King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 五年，勒死，子大雅僭立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Le died; his son Daya usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Le died, and his son Daya usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆死，子元真代立。

translations.literal: Murong Hui died; his son Yuanzhen succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui died, and his son Yuanzhen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 六年，石虎廢大雅，僭立。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shi Hu deposed Daya and usurped the throne himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shi Hu deposed Daya and usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 李雄死，兄子班立。

translations.literal: Li Xiong died; his elder brother's son Ban succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong died, and his elder brother's son Ban succeeded.

sentences.zh: 雄子期，殺班自立。

translations.literal: Xiong's son Qi killed Ban and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's son Qi killed Ban and seized the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 七年，藹頭不修臣職，召而戮之，國人復貳。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Aitou failed to perform his duties as subject; summoned and executed, the people of the state again grew divided in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Aitou neglected his duties as a subject. Summoned and executed, the people of the state again turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 煬帝自宇文部還入，諸部大人復奉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang returned from the Yuwen tribe; the great ladies of the tribes again upheld him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang returned from the Yuwen tribe, and the great ladies of the tribes again upheld him.

sentences.zh: 煬皇帝復立，以七年為後元年。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was restored; the seventh year was taken as the first year after restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was restored to the throne, and the seventh year was reckoned the first year of his second reign.

sentences.zh: 烈帝出居於鄴，石虎奉第宅、伎妾、奴婢、什物。

translations.literal: Emperor Lie went out to dwell at Ye; Shi Hu provided mansions, entertainers, servants, and sundry goods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lie went out to live at Ye, where Shi Hu furnished him with mansions, concubines, servants, and household goods.

sentences.zh: 三年，石虎遣將李穆率騎五千納烈帝於大寧，國人六千餘落叛煬帝，煬帝出居於慕容部。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi Hu sent the general Li Mu leading five thousand horse to install Emperor Lie at Daning; more than six thousand households of the people rebelled against Emperor Yang, and Emperor Yang went out to dwell with the Murong tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi Hu sent General Li Mu with five thousand cavalry to install Emperor Lie at Daning. More than six thousand households rebelled against Emperor Yang, who went out to dwell with the Murong tribe.

sentences.zh: 烈皇帝復立，以三年為後元年。

translations.literal: Emperor Lie was restored; the third year was taken as the first year after restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lie was restored, and the third year was reckoned the first year of his second reign.

sentences.zh: 城新盛樂城，在故城東南十里。

translations.literal: They built the new city of Shengle, ten li southeast of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: They built the new city of Shengle, ten li southeast of the old capital.

sentences.zh: 一年而崩。

translations.literal: After one year he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇帝諱什翼犍立，平文之次子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng, taboo name Shiyijian, succeeded; he was the second son of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng, taboo name Shiyijian, succeeded; he was the second son of Emperor Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 生而奇偉，寬仁大度，喜怒不形于色。

translations.literal: From birth he was extraordinarily imposing, magnanimous and broad-minded; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was singular in stature, generous and forbearing; neither joy nor anger showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，隆準龍顏，立髮委地，臥則乳垂至席。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi in height, with a high nose and dragon countenance; hair hanging to the ground when standing, and when lying down his nipples reached the mat.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, with a high-bridged nose and a dragon-like face; standing, his hair trailed to the ground; lying down, his breasts hung to the mat.

sentences.zh: 烈帝臨崩顧命曰：「必迎立什翼犍，社稷可安。

translations.literal: Emperor Lie on his deathbed issued final charge: "You must welcome and install Shiyijian—then the altars of state may be secure."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Lie charged them: "You must welcome and enthrone Shiyijian—only then will the altars of state be secure."

sentences.zh: 」烈帝崩，帝弟孤乃自詣鄴奉迎，與帝俱還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lie died, the emperor's younger brother Gu went himself to Ye to welcome him and returned together with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lie died, the emperor's younger brother Gu went in person to Ye to welcome him home, and they returned together.

sentences.zh: 事在孤傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biography of Gu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，帝即位於繁畤之北，時年十九，稱建國元年。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the emperor took the throne north of Fandi; he was nineteen years old; it was called the first year of Jianguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor was enthroned north of Fandi. He was nineteen; the era was named Jianguo, year one.

sentences.zh: 是歲，李雄從弟壽殺期僭立，自號曰漢。

translations.literal: That year Li Xiong's younger cousin Shou killed Qi and usurped the throne, styling himself Han.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Xiong's younger cousin Shou killed Qi, usurped the throne, and styled his state Han.

sentences.zh: 二年春，始置百官，分掌眾職。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he first established the hundred offices, each administering its duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he first appointed the hundred offices, each to govern its charge.

sentences.zh: 東自濊貊，西及破洛那，莫不款附。

translations.literal: From the east from the Mohe lands to the west as far as Poluona, none failed to submit in goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: From the Mohe in the east to Poluona in the west, all came forward in submission.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，朝諸大人於參合陂，議欲定都灅源川，連日不決，乃從太后計而止。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer he convened the great ladies at Canhepo, deliberated on fixing the capital at Juanyuanchuan; for days no decision was reached, and they stopped upon following the empress dowager's plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he assembled the great ladies at Canhepo to debate moving the capital to Juanyuanchuan. For days they could not decide, and at last abandoned the plan on the empress dowager's advice.

sentences.zh: 語在皇后傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biography of the empress.

sentences.zh: 娉慕容元真妹為皇后。

translations.literal: He took as empress the younger sister of Murong Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He took Murong Yuanzhen's younger sister as empress.

sentences.zh: 三年春，移都於雲中之盛樂宮。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he moved the capital to the Shengle Palace in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he moved the capital to the Shengle Palace at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 四年秋九月，築盛樂城於故城南八里。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in the fourth year he built Shengle city eight li south of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn in the fourth year he built Shengle city eight li south of the old capital.

sentences.zh: 皇后慕容氏崩。

translations.literal: Empress Murong died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Murong died.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，劉虎寇西境。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Liu Hu raided the western border.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Liu Hu raided the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝遣軍逆討，大破之，虎僅以身免。

translations.literal: The emperor sent troops to meet and attack, routing them utterly; Hu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent troops to meet and attack him, winning a great victory; Hu barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 虎死，子務桓立，始來歸順，帝以女妻之。

translations.literal: When Hu died his son Wuhuan succeeded and first came to submit; the emperor gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu died, his son Wuhuan succeeded and first came to submit. The emperor gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 十二月，慕容元真遣使朝貢，并薦其宗女。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with tribute and also recommended a woman of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with tribute and also offered a clanswoman for the harem.

sentences.zh: 五年夏五月，幸參合陂。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the fifth year he visited Canhepo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the fifth year he visited Canhepo.

sentences.zh: 秋七月七日，諸部畢集，設壇埒，講武馳射，因以為常。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month of autumn all tribes assembled, set up the arena mound, held martial exercises and mounted archery—it thus became custom.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month in autumn all the tribes gathered. They set up the arena, drilled in arms, and held mounted archery—a custom thereafter observed every year.

sentences.zh: 八月，還雲中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，司馬衍死，弟岳僭立。

translations.literal: That autumn Sima Yan died; his younger brother Yue usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Sima Yan died, and his younger brother Yue usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 六年秋八月，慕容元真遣使請薦女。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the sixth year Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys requesting to present a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in the sixth year Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys asking to present a daughter.

sentences.zh: 是年，李壽死，子勢僭立，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Li Shou died; his son Shi usurped the throne and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Shou died. His son Shi usurped the throne and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年春二月，遣大人長孫秩迎后慕容氏元真之女於境。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring of the seventh year he sent the great lady Changsun Zhi to welcome the empress, daughter of Murong Yuanzhen of the Murong clan, at the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the seventh year he sent the great lady Changsun Zhi to the border to welcome the empress—Murong Yuanzhen's daughter.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，皇后至自和龍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer the empress arrived from Helong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer the empress arrived from Helong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，慕容元真遣使奉聘，求交婚，帝許之，九月，以烈帝女妻之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with betrothal gifts, seeking a marriage alliance; the emperor consented; in the ninth month he gave Emperor Lie's daughter to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with betrothal gifts, seeking a marriage alliance. The emperor agreed, and in the ninth month gave Emperor Lie's daughter to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 其年，司馬岳死，子聃僭立。

translations.literal: That year Sima Yue died; his son Dan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Yue died, and his son Dan usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 八年，慕容元真遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Murong Yuanzhen sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是年，張駿私署假涼王。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Jun privately styled himself Acting Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Jun privately styled himself Acting Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 九年，石虎遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Hu sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Shi Hu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是年，張駿死，子重華代立。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Jun died; his son Chonghua succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Jun died, and his son Chonghua succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十年，遣使詣鄴觀釁。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he sent envoys to Ye to observe signs of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he sent envoys to Ye to spy out the situation.

sentences.zh: 是年，司馬聃擒李勢。

translations.literal: That year Sima Dan captured Li Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Dan captured Li Shi.

sentences.zh: 張重華遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年，慕容元真死，子儁代立。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Murong Yuanzhen died; his son Jun succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Murong Yuanzhen died, and his son Jun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，西巡，至河而還。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he toured west, reached the river and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he toured west as far as the river and returned.

sentences.zh: 是年，石虎死，子世立。

translations.literal: That year Shi Hu died; his son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shi Hu died, and his son Shi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 世兄遵，殺世自立。

translations.literal: Shi's elder brother Zun killed Shi and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's elder brother Zun killed him and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 遵兄鑒，殺遵自立。

translations.literal: Zun's elder brother Jian killed Zun and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's elder brother Jian killed Zun and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 十三年，魏郡人冉閔，殺石鑒僭立。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Ran Min of Wei Commandery killed Shi Jian and usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Ran Min of Wei Commandery killed Shi Jian and usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四年，帝曰：「石胡衰滅，冉閔肆禍，中州紛梗，莫有匡救，吾將親率六軍，廓定四海。
