translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the emperor said: "The Shi barbarians wane and perish; Ran Min wreaks havoc; the Central Plains are in turmoil with none to set them right—I will personally lead the Six Armies and sweep the four seas clear."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the emperor declared: "The Shi are in decline, Ran Min runs riot, and the Central Plains are in chaos with no one to restore order. I shall personally lead the Six Armies and bring peace to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」乃敕諸部，各率所統，以俟大期。

translations.literal: He then ordered the various tribes, each to lead its forces, to await the great day.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered each tribe to muster its forces and await the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 諸大人諫曰：「今中州大亂，誠宜進取，如聞豪強並起，不可一舉而定，若或留連，經歷歲稔，恐無永逸之利，或有虧損之憂。

translations.literal: The great ladies remonstrated: "Now the Central Plains are in great disorder—it is indeed time to advance; yet we hear powerful lords rising together; they cannot be settled in one stroke. If we linger and years pass, I fear there will be no lasting benefit, or there may be worry of losses."
translations.idiomatic: The great ladies remonstrated: "The Central Plains are indeed in turmoil and ripe for conquest, but powerful rivals are rising on every side. They cannot be subdued at a single stroke. If we linger for years, we may forfeit lasting gain—or suffer real losses."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，氐苻健僭稱大位，自號大秦。

translations.literal: That year the Di chieftain Fu Jian usurped the great position and styled himself Great Qin.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Di leader Fu Jian usurped the imperial dignity and styled his state Great Qin.

sentences.zh: 十五年，慕容儁滅冉閔，僭尊號。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Murong Jun destroyed Ran Min and usurped honored title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Murong Jun destroyed Ran Min and usurped an imperial title.

sentences.zh: 十六年，慕容儁遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Murong Jun sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Murong Jun sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是年，張重華死，子曜靈立。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Chonghua died; his son Yaoling succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Chonghua died, and his son Yaoling succeeded.

sentences.zh: 重華庶兄祚殺曜靈而自立，稱涼公。

translations.literal: Chonghua's younger brother by a concubine Zuo killed Yaoling and installed himself, styling himself Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua's younger half-brother Zuo killed Yaoling, seized power, and styled himself Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遣使於慕容儁。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he sent envoys to Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he sent envoys to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 張祚復稱涼王，置百官，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo again styled himself Prince of Liang, established the hundred offices, and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo again styled himself Prince of Liang, set up the full bureaucracy, and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十八年，太后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Empress Dowager Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Empress Dowager Wang died.

sentences.zh: 是年，苻健死，子生僭立。

translations.literal: That year Fu Jian died; his son Sheng usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fu Jian died, and his son Sheng usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 羌姚襄自稱大將軍、大單于。

translations.literal: The Qiang chief Yao Xiang styled himself Grand General and Great Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang leader Yao Xiang styled himself Grand General and Great Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 張瓘、宋混殺張祚，立重華少子玄靖，稱涼王。

translations.literal: Zhang Guan and Song Hun killed Zhang Zuo, installed Chonghua's youngest son Xuanjing, and styled him Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan and Song Hun killed Zhang Zuo, enthroned Chonghua's youngest son Xuanjing, and styled him Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 十九年春正月，劉務桓死，其弟閼頭立，潛謀反叛。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the nineteenth year Liu Wuhuan died; his younger brother Yantou succeeded and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the nineteenth year Liu Wuhuan died. His younger brother Yantou succeeded and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝西巡，因而臨河，使人招喻，閼頭從命。

translations.literal: In the second month the emperor toured west, and coming to the river sent men to summon and instruct; Yantou obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor toured west. Reaching the river, he sent men to summon and reassure Yantou, who submitted.

sentences.zh: 冬，慕容儁來請婚，許之。

translations.literal: In winter Murong Jun came requesting marriage; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Murong Jun sought a marriage alliance, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏五月，慕容儁奉納禮幣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the twentieth year Murong Jun presented betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the twentieth year Murong Jun presented betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 是年，苻堅殺苻生而僭立。

translations.literal: That year Fu Jian killed Fu Sheng and usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fu Jian killed Fu Sheng and usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 姚襄為苻眉所殺。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang was killed by Fu Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang was killed by Fu Mei.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，閼頭部民多叛，懼而東走。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year many of Yantou's tribesmen rebelled; fearing this he fled east.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year many of Yantou's people rebelled. In fear he fled eastward.

sentences.zh: 渡河，半濟而冰陷，後眾盡歸閼頭兄子悉勿祈。

translations.literal: He crossed the river; halfway across the ice gave way, and the men behind all went over to Yantou's elder brother's son Xiwuqi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river, but halfway across the ice broke through; the troops behind all went over to Yantou's elder brother's son Xiwuqi.

sentences.zh: 初，閼頭之叛，悉勿祈兄弟十二人在帝左右，盡遣歸，欲其自相猜離，至是，悉勿祈奪其眾。

translations.literal: At first when Yantou rebelled, Xiwuqi and his twelve brothers were at the emperor's side; all were sent back, intending that they would suspect and divide one another—now Xiwuqi seized his following.
translations.idiomatic: When Yantou first rebelled, Xiwuqi and his twelve brothers had been at the emperor's side; the emperor sent them all home, hoping they would turn on one another. Now Xiwuqi seized Yantou's followers.

sentences.zh: 閼頭窮而歸命，帝待之如初。

translations.literal: Yantou, reduced to extremity, came to submit; the emperor treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yantou, brought to bay, submitted again; the emperor treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，帝東巡，至於桑乾川。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year the emperor toured east as far as Sanggan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year the emperor toured east to the Sanggan River.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容儁遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third month Murong Jun sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Murong Jun sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，帝還雲中。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer the emperor returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the emperor returned to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 悉勿祈死，弟衞辰立。

translations.literal: Xiwuqi died; his younger brother Weichen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwuqi died, and his younger brother Weichen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，衞辰遣子朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Weichen sent his son with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Weichen sent his son with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三年夏六月，皇后慕容氏崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-third year Empress Murong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-third year Empress Murong died.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，衞辰來會葬，因而求婚，許之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Weichen came to attend the funeral and sought a marriage alliance; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Weichen came for the funeral and sought a marriage alliance; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 是歲，慕容儁死，子暐立，遣使致賻。

translations.literal: That year Murong Jun died; his son Wei succeeded and sent envoys with funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Jun died. His son Wei succeeded and sent envoys with funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，衞辰遣使朝聘。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year Weichen sent envoys on a court visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year Weichen sent envoys on a court visit.

sentences.zh: 是年，司馬聃死，衍子千齡僭立。

translations.literal: That year Sima Dan died; Yan's son Qianling usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Dan died, and Yan's son Qianling usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，帝南巡，至君子津。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor toured south as far as Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor toured south to Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，行幸代。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he traveled to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he traveled to Dai.

sentences.zh: 十一月，慕容暐薦女備後宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Murong Wei recommended a daughter for the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Murong Wei offered a daughter for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 二十六年冬十月，帝討高車，大破之，獲萬口，馬牛羊百餘萬頭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter of the twenty-sixth year the emperor attacked the Gaoche, routing them utterly; captives numbered ten thousand mouths, horses, cattle, and sheep more than a million head.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter of the twenty-sixth year the emperor attacked the Gaoche and won a great victory, taking ten thousand captives and more than a million head of horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 是年，張重華弟天錫殺玄靖而自立。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Chonghua's younger brother Tianshi killed Xuanjing and seized power himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Chonghua's younger brother Tianshi killed Xuanjing and seized power.

sentences.zh: 二十七年春，車駕還雲中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year the imperial carriage returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year the imperial carriage returned to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，討沒歌部，破之，獲牛馬羊數百萬頭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter he attacked the Moge tribe, defeated them, and took several million head of cattle, horses, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he attacked the Moge tribe, defeated them, and took several million head of cattle, horses, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春正月，衞辰謀反，東渡河。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed the river eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed the river to the east.

sentences.zh: 帝討之，衞辰懼而遁走。

translations.literal: The emperor attacked him; Weichen, in fear, fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attacked him, and Weichen fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，苻堅遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Fu Jian sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter Fu Jian sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，司馬千齡死，弟弈僭立。

translations.literal: That year Sima Qianling died; his younger brother Yi usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Qianling died, and his younger brother Yi usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十九年夏五月，遣燕鳳使苻堅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the twenty-ninth year he sent Yan Feng as envoy to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer of the twenty-ninth year he sent Yan Feng as envoy to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 三十年冬十月，帝征衞辰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter of the thirtieth year the emperor campaigned against Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter of the thirtieth year the emperor campaigned against Weichen.

sentences.zh: 時河冰未成，帝乃以葦絙約澌，俄然冰合，猶未能堅，乃散葦於上，冰草相結，如浮橋焉。

translations.literal: At that time the river ice had not yet formed; the emperor bound the slush with reed ropes, and presently the ice joined; it was still not firm, so he scattered reeds on top—the ice and reeds bound together like a floating bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The river had not yet frozen solid. The emperor bound the slush with reed ropes until the ice suddenly joined; still not firm enough, he scattered reeds upon it until ice and grass knit together like a floating bridge.

sentences.zh: 眾軍利涉，出其不意，衞辰與宗族西走，收其部落而還，俘獲生口及馬牛羊數十萬頭。

translations.literal: The army crossed with ease, taking the enemy unawares; Weichen fled west with his clansmen; they gathered his tribes and returned, capturing people and several hundred thousand head of horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed with ease and took the enemy unawares. Weichen fled west with his clan; the emperor gathered up his tribes and returned with captives and several hundred thousand head of horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春，帝至自西伐，班賞各有差。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-first year the emperor returned from the western campaign and distributed rewards according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-first year the emperor returned from the western campaign and distributed rewards according to merit.

sentences.zh: 三十二年正月，帝南幸君子津。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-second year the emperor traveled south to Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-second year the emperor traveled south to Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，幸代。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he visited Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he visited Dai.

sentences.zh: 三十三年冬十一月，征高車，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter of the thirty-third year he campaigned against the Gaoche and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter of the thirty-third year he campaigned against the Gaoche and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 是年，苻堅擒慕容暐。

translations.literal: That year Fu Jian captured Murong Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fu Jian captured Murong Wei.

sentences.zh: 三十四年春，長孫斤謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 斤之反也，拔刃向御座，太子獻明皇帝諱寔格之，傷脅。

translations.literal: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the imperial seat; the crown prince, the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi, blocked him and was wounded in the flank.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the throne; the crown prince—the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi—blocked him and was wounded in the flank.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，薨，後追諡焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer he died; posthumous title was conferred afterward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he died; a posthumous title was conferred later.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，皇孫珪生，大赦。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是年，司馬弈臣桓溫，廢弈為海西公，立叡子昱。

translations.literal: That year the minister Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and installed Rui's son Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and enthroned Rui's son Yu.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，司馬昱死，子昌明僭立。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died; his son Changming usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died, and his son Changming usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 三十六年夏五月，遣燕鳳使苻堅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the thirty-sixth year he sent Yan Feng as envoy to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer of the thirty-sixth year he sent Yan Feng as envoy to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，帝征衞辰，衞辰南走。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year the emperor campaigned against Weichen; Weichen fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year the emperor campaigned against Weichen, and Weichen fled south.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，衞辰求援於苻堅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year Weichen sought aid from Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year Weichen sought aid from Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，苻堅遣其大司馬苻洛率眾二十萬及朱彤、張蚝、鄧羌等諸道來寇，侵逼南境。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Fu Jian sent his Grand Marshal Fu Luo leading two hundred thousand troops, with Zhu Tong, Zhang Hao, Deng Qiang, and others on various routes to invade, pressing the southern border.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year Fu Jian sent his Grand Marshal Fu Luo at the head of two hundred thousand men, with Zhu Tong, Zhang Hao, Deng Qiang, and others on several routes to invade and press the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，白部、獨孤部禦之，敗績。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter the Bai and Dugu tribes met them in defense and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter the Bai and Dugu tribes met them in defense and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 南部大人劉庫仁走雲中。

translations.literal: The southern great lady Liu Kuren fled to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The southern great lady Liu Kuren fled to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣庫仁率騎十萬逆戰於石子嶺，王師不利。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Kuren leading one hundred thousand horse to meet battle at Shizi Ridge; the royal army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Kuren with one hundred thousand cavalry to meet them at Shizi Ridge; the royal army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝時不豫，羣臣莫可任者，乃率國人避於陰山之北。

translations.literal: The emperor was then unwell; among ministers none could be entrusted—he therefore led the people of the state to take refuge north of Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then ill, and no minister seemed fit for the task; he therefore led the people north of Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 高車雜種盡叛，四面寇鈔，不得芻牧。

translations.literal: Mixed Gaoche tribes all rebelled; raiders pressed from every side, and they could not pasture or gather fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed Gaoche tribes all rebelled; raiders closed in from every side, and they could neither pasture nor gather fodder.

sentences.zh: 復度漠南。

translations.literal: They again crossed south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed south of the desert again.

sentences.zh: 堅軍稍退，乃還。

translations.literal: Jian's army gradually withdrew, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: As Jian's army gradually withdrew, they returned.

sentences.zh: 十二月，至雲中，旬有二日，帝崩，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they reached Yunzhong; twelve days later the emperor died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they reached Yunzhong. Twelve days later the emperor died, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，尊曰高祖。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he was honored as Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, he was posthumously honored as Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 帝雅性寬厚，智勇仁恕。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature magnanimous, wise, brave, and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature magnanimous, wise, brave, and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 時國中少繒帛，代人許謙盜絹二匹，守者以告，帝匿之，謂燕鳳曰：「吾不忍視謙之面，卿勿泄言，謙或慚而自殺，為財辱士，非也。

translations.literal: At that time the state had little silk; the Dai man Xu Qian stole two bolts, and the guards reported it. The emperor concealed it and said to Yan Feng: "I cannot bear to look upon Qian's face—do not let word out. Qian may be shamed into killing himself; to disgrace a gentleman for property is not right."
translations.idiomatic: Silk was scarce in the realm. A man of Dai named Xu Qian stole two bolts; the guards reported him. The emperor hushed the matter and told Yan Feng: "I cannot bear to look Qian in the face—say nothing. He may be shamed into taking his own life; to ruin a gentleman over money would be wrong."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗擊西部叛賊，流矢中目。

translations.literal: The emperor once attacked rebel bandits in the west; a stray arrow struck his eye.
translations.idiomatic: Once, campaigning against rebels in the west, a stray arrow struck his eye.

sentences.zh: 賊破之後，諸大臣執射者，各持錐刀欲屠割之。

translations.literal: After the bandits were broken, the great ministers seized the archer, each holding awl and knife intending to butcher him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were broken, the great ministers seized the archer; each held awl and knife, ready to butcher him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼各為其主，何罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Each served his own lord—what crime is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Each man served his own lord—what crime is that?"

sentences.zh: 」乃釋之。

translations.literal: He then released them.
translations.idiomatic: He released them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，苻堅滅張天錫。

translations.literal: That year Fu Jian destroyed Zhang Tianshi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fu Jian destroyed Zhang Tianshi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：帝王之興也，必有積德累功博利，道協幽顯，方契神祇之心。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When emperors and kings rise, there must be accumulated virtue, piled merit, and broad benefit; the Way accords with what is hidden and manifest, and only then does it match the heart of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When emperors and kings rise, they must have accumulated virtue, heaped merit, and broad benefit; only when the Way accords with what is hidden and manifest does it win the hearts of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 有魏奄迹幽方，世居君長，淳化育民，與時無競。

translations.literal: Wei held the traces of rule in the dark north, generation upon generation dwelling as chieftains, cultivating the people in simplicity, not contending with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held the north in quiet sovereignty, generation after generation as chieftains, nurturing the people in simplicity and not contending with the age.

sentences.zh: 神元生自天女，桓、穆勤於晉室。

translations.literal: Shenyuan was born of the heavenly woman; Huan and Mu were diligent toward the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan was born of a heavenly woman; Huan and Mu were diligent in the service of Jin.

sentences.zh: 靈心人事，夫豈徒然。

translations.literal: Spirit and human affairs in accord—was this merely chance?
translations.idiomatic: Spirit and human affairs working together—was that mere chance?

sentences.zh: 昭成以雄傑之姿，包君子之量，征伐四克，威被荒遐，乃立號改都，恢隆大業。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng, with heroic bearing and a gentleman's measure, conquered on every campaign and spread awe to the far marches; he then established title, changed the capital, and enlarged the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng, in heroic stature and with a gentleman's breadth, conquered wherever he marched and spread awe to the far marches; he established a reign title, moved the capital, and enlarged the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 終於百六十載，光宅區中。

translations.literal: In the end, through one hundred sixty years, they illuminated the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, through one hundred sixty years, they held the central realm.

sentences.zh: 其原固有由矣。

translations.literal: The origin indeed had its reasons.
translations.idiomatic: The origin indeed had its reasons.
